scope: Five cloud-practitioner extra questions reviewed against their linked AWS primary documentation. These are agent-assisted source and editorial checks, not official exam-owner validation or independent human sign-off.

records.sourceInspection: The linked official AWS documentation snapshot in tmp/reference-review was read for the stated claim. Each option and its explanation were assessed. No official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Correct: a workload role supplies temporary credentials, while scoped permissions address the approved bucket access requirement.
Incorrect: renaming a stored administrator key changes neither its long-lived nature nor its broad permission scope.
Incorrect: sharing one administrator key across workloads increases credential exposure and prevents workload-specific access boundaries.
records.scope: Reviews the stated AWS workload credential and permission direction against IAM security best practices. It does not assess bucket-policy details, deployment-specific role delivery, or independently validate an exam objective.

records.sourceInspection: The linked official AWS documentation snapshot in tmp/reference-review was read for the stated claim. Each option and its explanation were assessed. No official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Correct: AWS Budgets supports configured notifications for forecasted cost before the target is reached.
Incorrect: instance placement determines where compute runs and does not report forecast spending against a cost budget.
Incorrect: a recovery restore test evaluates recovery capability and is unrelated to cost forecast notifications.
records.scope: Checks whether AWS Budgets supports notifications for forecasted cost against a monthly target. It does not claim alerts are immediate or that a notification prevents spending.

records.sourceInspection: The linked official AWS documentation snapshot in tmp/reference-review was read for the stated claim. Each option and its explanation were assessed. No official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: idempotent handling is the recommended response to possible repeat delivery, not an assumption to avoid.
Incorrect: deduplicating repeated business intent can be a relevant application safeguard, depending on the processing design.
Correct: receiving a message does not prove it is a new intent; standard queues can redeliver a previously processed message.
records.scope: Checks the at-least-once delivery property documented for Amazon SQS standard queues and its application-design implication. It does not prescribe a specific deduplication store or transaction design.

records.sourceInspection: The linked official AWS documentation snapshot in tmp/reference-review was read for the stated claim. Each option and its explanation were assessed. No official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Correct: AWS recommends regularly reviewing and removing unused permissions to reduce unnecessary access.
Correct: IAM guidance recommends temporary role credentials for workloads instead of distributing long-lived credentials.
Incorrect: retaining unrelated permissions avoids the stated access review and leaves unnecessary access in place.
records.scope: Checks the two selected IAM practices against AWS IAM guidance: review unused access and use temporary role credentials for supported workloads. It does not evaluate the deployment-specific migration steps.

records.sourceInspection: The linked official AWS documentation snapshot in tmp/reference-review was read for the stated claim. Each option and its explanation were assessed. No official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: AWS documents data and billing delays; a budget notification can arrive after more charges accrue and is not a hard real-time spend cap.
Correct: the team must configure suitable thresholds and take appropriate action; notification alone does not eliminate cost-management responsibility.
Correct: AWS Budgets supports optional notifications for actual costs and forecasted overspend, subject to documented update and billing delays.
records.scope: Checks budget alert expectations against AWS Budgets documentation, including notification delay and possible additional spend. It does not assess budget actions or guarantee a specific notification delivery time.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 1 guide snapshot supports this as a learning-types objective. AWS Amazon ML guide defines supervised learning as learning from examples with known labels and gives spam/not-spam as its example: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/machine-learning-problems-in-amazon-machine-learning.html
choiceChecks: Correct: labeled spam and not-spam examples provide target outputs for a supervised classification task.
Incorrect: clustering groups observations by similarity without using the supplied labels as prediction targets.
Incorrect: reinforcement learning is characterized by reward-driven interaction; this scenario supplies labeled examples instead.
Incorrect: fixed hand-authored rules may classify messages but do not learn a mapping from labeled training examples.
records.scope: Checks the basic distinction between learning a classifier from labeled examples and the listed alternatives. The AWS exam guide confirms the objective coverage; AWS ML documentation supports the definition. No algorithm-specific claim is made.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 1 guide snapshot confirms the exam objective includes choosing techniques such as regression, classification, and clustering. AWS Amazon ML documentation describes regression as predicting a numeric value: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/machine-learning-problems-in-amazon-machine-learning.html
choiceChecks: Incorrect: clustering can group similar deliveries but does not directly produce the requested numeric delivery-time prediction.
Incorrect: image generation creates visual content and does not estimate a numeric delivery time.
Incorrect: on-time versus late is categorical classification, while the question asks for a numeric time estimate.
Correct: regression is the listed task for predicting a numeric or continuous quantity such as delivery time.
records.scope: Checks whether the requested continuous numeric estimate is a regression task. The AWS AIF-C01 guide lists regression and clustering as task-selection concepts; an AWS ML source provides their task distinction.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 1 guide snapshot includes model lifecycle and evaluation objectives. AWS documentation says evaluation on training data does not establish generalization and recommends held-out evaluation data: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/splitting-the-data-into-training-and-evaluation-data.html
choiceChecks: Incorrect: the classifier still uses labels as targets; evaluating on training examples does not remove the need for them.
Incorrect: reusing training examples for evaluation does not guarantee absence of leakage and can obscure it.
Correct: training-set results alone do not estimate performance on unseen examples; held-out data is needed for that evaluation.
Incorrect: a perfect result on seen examples does not establish perfect deployment performance on future inputs.
records.scope: Checks the limitation of evaluating only on training examples. The prompt asks about evidence for performance on unseen examples; it does not imply that all training-set evaluation is useless for every diagnostic purpose.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 1 guide snapshot includes model-performance metrics. AWS SageMaker AI metrics reference defines recall as TP/(TP+FN), the fraction of actual positives correctly identified: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas-metrics.html
choiceChecks: Incorrect: training cost is an economic measure and does not count how many actual positives the classifier finds.
Correct: recall divides true positives by all actual positives (true positives plus false negatives), matching the requested fraction.
Incorrect: precision measures the reliability of predicted positives, not the share of actual positives found.
Incorrect: inference latency measures response time and says nothing about the fraction of actual positive cases detected.
records.scope: Checks the conventional recall definition for binary classification in the stated true-positive setting. The question asks which metric measures coverage of actual positives, not which metric is best for every screening decision.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 1 guide snapshot explicitly includes identifying when AI/ML is not appropriate, including when a specific outcome is required instead of a prediction. The source supports the scenario’s governing constraint: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain1.html
choiceChecks: Correct: a deterministic implementation directly satisfies a fully specified exact calculation without introducing an unnecessary prediction step.
Incorrect: the prompt requires an exact known rule, so choosing a generative model merely because it is available adds no fit-for-purpose benefit.
Incorrect: clustering discovers groups and does not implement the exact formula the business already specified.
Incorrect: creative sampling introduces variability where the requirement is a fixed, exact result.
records.scope: Checks the choice to use an exact deterministic rule when the required result is fully specified. It does not claim that AI is never useful alongside deterministic logic in a larger system.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 2 guide snapshot lists generating content as a GenAI use case. AWS Bedrock documentation describes foundation models generating varied responses for use cases: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/foundation-models-reference.html
choiceChecks: Incorrect: retrieval returns content that already exists; the scenario says the assistant creates a new draft.
Incorrect: assigning topic labels is a classification task and does not compose new text.
Incorrect: similarity ranking orders stored drafts rather than generating the requested new content.
Correct: producing a new draft from an instruction illustrates generative AI content generation.
records.scope: Checks the distinction between composing new content and retrieving or organizing existing content. The scenario is about the capability illustrated, not the quality or factuality of the generated draft.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 2 guide snapshot includes hallucinations and inaccuracy among GenAI disadvantages. AWS Prescriptive Guidance defines hallucination as confidently generated incorrect or fabricated information: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pdfs/prescriptive-guidance/latest/strategy-data-considerations-gen-ai/strategy-data-considerations-gen-ai.pdf
choiceChecks: Incorrect: the prompt describes an invented identifier, not merely a formatting problem with a supported policy reference.
Incorrect: the fabricated identifier provides no evidence about encryption configuration or data at rest.
Correct: inventing a nonexistent factual identifier is fabricated output, which AWS describes as a hallucination.
Incorrect: because the policy number does not exist, the response cannot be considered a faithful restatement of verified information.
records.scope: Checks hallucination as a limitation illustrated by a fluent but fabricated identifier. It does not assert that every unsupported answer has the same cause or that hallucinations are always fluent.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 2 guide snapshot includes token-based pricing and its effect on inference cost. Amazon Bedrock cost documentation states charges depend on token type and separately accounts for input and output tokens: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-understanding-cur-data.html
choiceChecks: Incorrect: model storage footprint is unrelated to the stated token-based charges for long prompts and generated answers.
Correct: input and output token counts are direct billing dimensions for token-priced inference and both are large in the scenario.
Incorrect: first-token latency measures response speed, not the number of billable input and output tokens.
Incorrect: user count alone ignores request size, which the scenario identifies as long on both input and output.
records.scope: Checks the stated token-priced inference cost driver. It avoids comparing exact prices, which vary by model, region, tier, and pricing arrangement.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 2 guide lists Amazon Bedrock among services for GenAI applications. The current Amazon Bedrock overview describes it as a fully managed service providing access to foundation models: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/bedrock/latest/userguide/what-is-bedrock.html
choiceChecks: Correct: Amazon Bedrock is AWS’s managed service for accessing foundation models for generative AI applications.
Incorrect: SageMaker AI supports custom ML workflows, but the scenario specifically asks for managed foundation-model access without deploying endpoints.
Incorrect: S3 stores objects and input documents; it does not itself provide model inference.
Incorrect: OpenSearch supports search and retrieval; it is not the managed foundation-model inference service requested.
records.scope: Checks the requested managed foundation-model access service among the listed AWS options. It does not imply that Bedrock is the right service for every custom machine-learning workflow.

records.sourceInspection: AWS AIF-C01 Domain 2 guide identifies MCP’s role in connecting agents to external systems. AWS Prescriptive Guidance describes MCP as a standardized tool-integration protocol and separately emphasizes authentication and authorization: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/agentic-ai-frameworks/tool-integration-strategy.html
choiceChecks: Incorrect: a connection protocol does not guarantee that each proposed tool action is authorized; permission checks remain necessary.
Incorrect: MCP integration does not replace application authentication or the tool’s authorization controls.
Incorrect: standardizing tool connections does not eliminate errors in model-generated reasoning or outputs.
Correct: Model Context Protocol is the integration concept for connecting an AI assistant to external tools and context.
records.scope: Checks MCP’s role in connecting agents to external tools and context. The question asks for the integration concept, not a security guarantee; the distractors explicitly test that MCP does not itself replace authorization, application authentication, or model-quality controls.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain3.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-how-it-works.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: display resolution changes presentation and supplies no relevant passages from the private manuals.
Incorrect: randomly changing weights is not a retrieval method and would make behavior less controlled.
Correct: RAG retrieves relevant source content and adds it to the model context at inference time.
Incorrect: pretraining cannot ensure access to future revisions of private documents.
records.scope: Checks why RAG is suited to frequently updated private-source context at inference time. It does not imply retrieved material is always complete, current, authorized, or correct.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain3.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: the prompt explicitly includes examples, so it is not deleting all context.
Correct: several demonstrations included in a prompt are few-shot prompting (also called in-context learning).
Incorrect: examples in an inference prompt do not describe training a model from scratch.
Incorrect: the examples show a desired output pattern rather than an unsupervised grouping task.
records.scope: Checks the name for examples supplied inside the prompt. It does not claim that examples guarantee better output or that prompt examples retrain model weights.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain3.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-models.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Correct: supervised fine-tuning uses training examples and adjusts model parameters for represented tasks.
Incorrect: retrieval supplies documents as context; it does not itself update model parameters.
Incorrect: a website color change has no relationship to training model parameters.
Incorrect: a hyperlink alone provides no training examples or parameter update.
records.scope: Checks the defining parameter-update aspect of supervised fine-tuning against retrieval and irrelevant presentation changes. It does not claim fine-tuning is always preferable to retrieval.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain3.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/evaluation.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: perceived confidence is not a comparable measure of whether business tasks were completed.
Incorrect: changing test questions for just one assistant confounds the comparison.
Incorrect: one easy success case cannot represent the stipulated representative workload.
Correct: applying consistent task-quality and business-constraint measures to the same representative tasks supports a useful comparison.
records.scope: Checks the need for a controlled comparison using representative common tasks and criteria tied to business quality and constraints. It does not prescribe a universal metric or claim one evaluation set proves production suitability.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain5.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/agentic-ai-frameworks/security-best-practices-for-tool-integration.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: record existence does not establish that the caller is authorized to modify it.
Incorrect: valid JSON checks argument syntax, not whether the requested action is permitted.
Correct: the model’s proposed action and the application’s authorization decision are separate; permission must be checked before execution.
Incorrect: an explanation or formatting detail does not establish permission to perform an action.
records.scope: Checks separation of model proposal from execution authorization for a tool capable of changing records. It does not specify a particular identity provider, policy engine, or approval workflow.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain4.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-measure-post-training-bias.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: deleting failures removes evidence and can distort the evaluation.
Correct: disaggregate performance and investigate affected cases; the observed disparity warrants inquiry but does not alone prove its cause.
Incorrect: hiding subgroup outcomes prevents the team from assessing the reported risk.
Incorrect: a high aggregate can mask relevant subgroup error differences and does not by itself establish fairness.
records.scope: Checks the need to examine relevant subgroup behavior when aggregate accuracy hides a disparity. The disparity is a signal to investigate; this review does not infer its cause or prescribe a fairness threshold.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain4.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-cards.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Correct: documenting intended uses, evaluation evidence, and limitations helps communicate the model’s behavior and scope.
Incorrect: documentation cannot guarantee that every future prediction is correct.
Incorrect: publishing documentation does not eliminate the need for context-appropriate human review.
Incorrect: a model description is not automatic legal approval for every use.
records.scope: Checks transparency through intended-use, evaluation, and limitation documentation. Documentation supports informed review but is not proof of correctness, safety, or legal approval.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain4.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: adding guardrails does not prove that harmful outputs are impossible.
Incorrect: content filters do not substitute for data access authorization and permissions.
Incorrect: guardrails can help detect/filter some risks but do not guarantee perfect factual accuracy.
Correct: treat guardrails as controls to configure and evaluate alongside other safeguards, not as guarantees.
records.scope: Checks guardrails as risk-reduction controls that require use-case evaluation. It does not claim every filter fails, nor specify an exhaustive defense design.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain4.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-measure-post-training-bias.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: dataset gaps strengthen the need to evaluate; they do not justify ignoring evaluation.
Incorrect: branding has no effect on whether the population is represented in the data.
Correct: an omitted intended-use population raises a representativeness and inclusivity concern requiring investigation.
Incorrect: file-name length does not address who is or is not represented in the dataset.
records.scope: Checks representativeness when an intended-use population is absent from a dataset. It does not establish a measured impact without evaluation on relevant data.

records.sourceInspection: Read the current AWS AIF-C01 domain guide for the objective and the directly relevant AWS primary documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain4.html | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-model-explainability.html. The sources support the concept and option distinctions described here; no official exam endorsement or independent human validation is claimed.
choiceChecks: Incorrect: explanations can aid understanding but do not remove every model or decision risk.
Correct: an explanation should be useful for its audience and supported by the explanation method and available evidence.
Incorrect: presenting an invented narrative as the model’s exact internal process would be misleading.
Incorrect: a confidence value alone may not explain the factors or comparison relevant to the recommendation.
records.scope: Checks that explanations should be meaningful and evidence-grounded rather than invented as exact internal cognition. AWS Clarify is one attribution method and, per current docs, no longer open to new customers; the concept here is general.
